name: Unity Catalog (lakehouse engine)
shared_by: lakehouse engine source (AWS Glue, Iceberg REST or Unity Catalog)

companions.name: LAKEHOUSE_DISTRIBUTE_FILES
companions.body:
function run(ctx)
    repeat
        ctx.emit(ctx.files)
    until not ctx.next()
end

inputs.name: namespace
inputs.label: Schema as catalog.schema (e.g. main.sales; one schema is one virtual schema)

inputs.name: region
inputs.label: AWS region of the bucket that holds the tables (e.g. us-east-2)

access: USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA, SELECT and EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA on the schema, with External Data Access switched on for the metastore
auth_hint: a Databricks personal access token (Settings, Developer, Access tokens) of a user who may read the schema
tips: Names arrive in upper case (ORDERS, ORDER_ID): no quotes needed.

The schema must sit on your own cloud storage with External Data Access allowed (and EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA granted); a schema on Databricks Default Storage cannot be read from outside - use exakit connect databricks for it.
Databricks catalog-managed tables cannot be read by this adapter version: read those through the SQL warehouse with exakit connect databricks.
notes: The Glue lakehouse connector's engine over Unity Catalog (Databricks or OSS): the same pinned lakehouse-engine-rs build, scripts and Rust language container, shared with Glue and Iceberg REST sources.

The CONNECTION goes TO the workspace URL with an empty user; its password is JSON the kit writes: the token, use_vended_credentials and the region. Unity's temporary storage credentials carry no region, so the bucket's region is asked for, not guessed.

The rows are read from storage by the engine inside this database, not by a Databricks warehouse: nothing runs on Databricks compute. exakit connect databricks is the other route, through the SQL warehouse.
